characters.name: Savitri
characters.look: Royal young woman in simple forest sari, steady eyes

characters.name: Satyavan
characters.look: Strong young man in ascetic clothes, short beard

characters.name: Yama
characters.look: Tall red-robed figure with a coiled noose, calm but exact

lines.text: A princess married a man doomed to die in one year. She read fine print.

look.note: Savitri stands in the courtyard, holding a palm leaf

lines.text: Princess Savitri chose her own husband rather than having one arranged for her.

look.note: Savitri faces the courtyard gate, determined

lines.text: The sage warned that Satyavan had one defect: he would die within a year, but Savitri refused to choose twice.

look.note: Savitri listens by the banyan tree, arms folded

lines.text: Savitri married Satyavan in the forest hermitage and lived there as an ascetic, counting every day until the promised death date.

look.note: They walk together near the hut, Savitri glancing at the sky

lines.text: On the predicted day, Satyavan went into the forest to cut wood, and Savitri insisted on going with him.

look.note: Satyavan carries an axe, Savitri matches his pace

lines.text: Satyavan grew weak and laid his head in Savitri's lap; then Yama himself appeared in red, carrying a noose.

look.note: Satyavan lies pale, Yama steps out from the trees

lines.text: Savitri asked Yama why he came in person instead of sending his usual messengers; he told her to turn back.

look.note: Yama points back, Savitri stands firm

lines.text: She refused, arguing that seven steps with someone creates friendship, so Yama offered her any boon except her husband's life.

look.note: Savitri holds up seven fingers, Yama tilts his head

lines.text: Luckily, Savitri had already read the terms and conditions; she asked for her blind father-in-law's sight as her first wish.

look.note: Savitri counts one on her fingers, Yama listens

lines.text: Unluckily, Yama kept granting wishes, so she asked for her father-in-law's lost kingdom and then a hundred sons for her father.

look.note: Savitri adds wishes on her fingers, Yama nods slowly

lines.text: It was like a loyalty programme: every clever answer earned a wish, but the catalogue excluded her husband's life.

look.note: Savitri gestures like reading fine print

lines.text: She kept adding family benefits: sight, a kingdom, a hundred sons for her father, stacking small asks before the big one.

look.note: Savitri ticks items off on her fingers

lines.text: Then she asked for a hundred sons for herself and Satyavan though he was dead—trap no fine print could dodge.
She pointed out the promised sons could not exist without their father, so Yama's own boon required Satyavan to live.

look.note: Savitri points at Satyavan's body, Yama frowns

lines.text: Yama conceded, untied his noose, and granted Satyavan a life of four hundred years.

look.note: Yama releases the noose, light returns to Satyavan

lines.text: Satyavan woke on her lap, thinking he had merely slept long, and asked where the dark figure had gone.

look.note: Satyavan sits up, rubbing his eyes; Savitri helps him

lines.text: The fine print didn't save him; she read it, argued every clause, and Yama signed the revised terms in red ink.

look.note: Savitri stands over Satyavan; Yama fades at the edge
